newsitem.title: GERMANY: SPD says German euro controversy is nonsense.
newsitem.headline: SPD says German euro controversy is nonsense.

text.p: German opposition leader Oskar Lafontaine said on Monday he believed a strict instistence on one of the key membership rules for European monetary union was "economic nonsense".

Lafontaine rejected Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber's calls for rigid adherence to the criterion which stipulates EMU members should have a budget deficit of not more than three percent of gross domestic product.

Stoiber wants three to be interpreted as 3.0 but Lafontaine, leader of the main opposition Social Democrats (SPD), said economic policy convergence and cooperation between EMU members was more important.
"This fetish for 3.0 is economic nonsense," Lafontaine told foreign journalists in Bonn. He declined to say what level of deficit should still be acceptable.
"If the project failed, it would be a setback for European unity," he added.

He acknowledged that Gerhard Schroeder, the premier of Lower Saxony state and possible rival to Lafontaine for the SPD chancellorship candidacy, favoured strict adherence to the criteria and a postponement of EMU if necessary.
But Lafontaine insisted this was not the view of the majority of the party.

Stoiber has threatened to vote against the single currency in the upper house of parliament if the deficit target is loosely interpreted but Lafontaine said he believed the project would find a majority in both the upper and the lower house.
